html:
Siad Barre was the army commander who seized power in Somalia in October 1969 and ruled it until he was driven out in January 1991.

He declared scientific socialism, allied with the Soviet Union, and gave Somali its first official script in 1972. He launched the Ogaden War against Ethiopia in 1977 to win the Somali lands there, and lost.

After defeat he turned to the West and relied more and more on his own clan. Rebel groups rose in the north and centre, and his forces bombed Hargeisa in the campaign against the Isaaq. When he fled Mogadishu the state collapsed into the civil war. He died in exile in Nigeria in 1995.
sum: Siad Barre was the army commander who seized power in Somalia in October 1969 and ruled it until he was driven out in January 1991.
